transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. Um, well... I'm a little embarrassed to even say it, to be honest. It's probably just stress, you know, being a tax preparer, work gets a bit overwhelming. But I keep having these... these weird moments. 

I hope I'm explaining this right, but sometimes my own house, or my office, it just feels completely unreal. It's almost like... like I'm watching myself from across the room instead of actually being there in my own body. 

I know that probably sounds really strange, and I'm sure it's nothing too serious, but... does that make sense? I just wanted to make sure I wasn't losing my mind or anything, if that's okay.
How long have you been experiencing these moments where things feel unreal?

Um, well, it hasn't been too long, really. Just... about two weeks? I hope I'm not wasting your time with this, because I know it's probably just a silly overreaction on my part. 

But it started right after this... um, this incident at work. A client got really upset and actually threatened me in my office. I'm sure he was just blowing off steam—you know how tax season makes people a little crazy—but ever since then, I've been having these episodes. 

Does that... does that sound like a normal reaction to you? Am I explaining that okay?
Have you experienced any hearing or seeing things that aren't there during these episodes?

Oh, no, no, nothing like that. I'm definitely not seeing or hearing things that aren't there. I mean, I know I said things feel unreal, but I'm not... I'm not hallucinating or anything crazy like that. 

I really hope I didn't give you the impression that I was losing touch with reality in that way. It's just that detached feeling I mentioned. Is that... is it okay that I don't have those symptoms? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Have you been feeling anxious or on edge since the incident at work?

Um, well... maybe just a little? I really don't want to sound paranoid or anything, and I'm sure it's just my nerves getting the better of me. But, yeah, I guess I have been a bit on edge. 

Like, even when I'm just relaxing at home in Roanoke, I catch myself... well, I keep tracking every car door that shuts outside, or every single footstep on the porch. And if I go out, I'm always looking for where the exits are. It's almost like I feel like I need to be ready for someone to come at me again. 

I know that probably sounds like a total overreaction, right? I mean, I logically know I'm safe. Does that make sense, though? I just hope I'm not making a bigger deal out of this than I should be, if that's okay to say.
Have you been avoiding certain places or situations since the incident at work?

Um, avoiding places? Well... no, not really. I mean, I'm still going to work every day, still seeing clients. I didn't want to let my boss down or make things harder for the rest of the team right in the middle of tax season. 

I guess... I mean, maybe I've been a little hesitant to take walk-in appointments if I don't recognize the name? But I haven't completely stopped doing my job or anything. I'm trying really hard to just push through it and be professional. 

I hope that's the right way to handle it? I just didn't want to be a burden or act like I couldn't do my job over one little scare. Is it normal that I'm still going in, or... should I be taking time off? I just want to do whatever you think is best.
Have you been avoiding any specific activities or tasks at work since the incident with the upset client?

Well, um... I know I just said I was still working, and I am, mostly... but I guess, if I'm being completely honest, there are a few things I've been struggling with. I really hope you don't think I'm just being lazy or unprofessional. 

It's just... I've actually missed a couple of client deadlines recently. I feel terrible about it, I really do. It's just so hard to focus, and I keep second-guessing all my calculations. I just don't trust myself to handle the returns properly right now, and I'd hate to make a mistake that costs a client money. 

And, um, I guess I kind of stopped seeing people in person at the office, too. I've been trying to do everything over the phone or email. I just... I don't feel like I can guarantee a safe environment right now, if that makes sense? I'm so sorry if that sounds like I'm not doing my job. I'm really trying my best to keep up. Is it okay that I'm taking a step back from face-to-face meetings for a bit? I just want to make sure I'm not doing the wrong thing.
Have you been avoiding social interactions outside of work since the incident?

Oh, um, no... I don't think so. I'm really trying hard not to let it affect my personal life, honestly. I still went over to my buddy's house to watch the game this past weekend. I mean, I might have been just a little quieter than usual, but I didn't cancel or anything. 

I feel like it's important to keep up with people, right? I definitely didn't want my friends to worry about me, or, you know, think I was being rude by blowing them off. I really want to show them I'm doing fine. 

Is it a good thing that I'm still trying to get out and see people? I just want to make sure I'm taking the right steps to get past this. I really hope I'm handling it the right way, if that makes sense.
Do you feel like these episodes and your reactions to the incident at work are significantly interfering with your ability to function in your daily life?

Well, um... "significantly interfering" sounds a little extreme, I guess. I really don't want you to think I'm completely falling apart or anything, because I am still trying my hardest to keep things normal. 

But... yeah, like I mentioned a few minutes ago, I guess it is taking a bit of a toll. Missing those client deadlines is just... it's really not like me at all. And since I stopped seeing people at the office, well, my whole routine is definitely messed up. I just don't trust myself to handle the returns right now without making a mistake, or to, you know, keep the workplace safe if someone were to come in. 

So, I suppose it is affecting my day-to-day more than I'd like to admit. I'm really sorry if it sounds like I'm failing at this... do you think I'm doing an okay job trying to manage it all, considering everything? I just really want to get back to being reliable again.
Are there any specific things that remind you of the incident with the upset client that you try to avoid thinking about or looking at?

Um, specific things? I don't... I don't really think so. I mean, I try not to dwell on the whole thing in general, of course, because I want to move past it and get back to being productive. But there isn't really one specific object or thought I'm constantly running away from, if that makes sense. 

I really try to keep a positive mindset, you know? I don't want to be the kind of person who just avoids everything. I hope that's a good sign? That I'm not, you know, obsessing over little details or anything like that.
Do you often find yourself thinking about the incident with the upset client when you're not trying to?

Um, thinking about it when I'm not trying to? No, not really. I mean, I really do my best to keep my mind occupied with other things, you know? I try to stay focused on the work I *can* do, or just, um, normal everyday stuff. 

I don't just sit around dwelling on it, I promise. I know that wouldn't be healthy or productive at all. I really try to just push it out of my head and look forward. I think I'm doing a pretty good job of just... keeping my thoughts in check. That's the right way to handle it, isn't it? Just trying to stay focused on the positive and not letting my mind wander back there?
Do you feel like you're experiencing a lot of distress because of these episodes and your reactions to the incident at work?

Well, um... "a lot of distress" might be a bit of a strong way to put it. I mean, I don't want to sound like I'm completely overwhelmed or anything. I'm really trying to keep a brave face and just push through, you know? 

I guess... well, I suppose it has been a little upsetting, sure. But I'm really trying not to let it get to me too much. I want to be strong and handle this the right way. I don't want to be a burden or seem like I can't cope with a little stress at work. 

I mean, everyone gets a little rattled sometimes, right? I'm just trying to stay positive and not let it drag me down. Do you think I'm handling it okay? I just really want to make sure I'm doing the right things to get back on track.
Do you find yourself trying to avoid thinking about the incident with the upset client?

Um, well... I know I mentioned a minute ago about trying to push it out of my head, but I wouldn't say I'm actively *avoiding* thinking about it, if that makes sense? Like, I'm not running away from the memory as if it terrifies me. 

I just... I choose not to dwell on it. I really don't want you to think I'm in denial or burying my head in the sand or anything like that. I just try to shift my focus back to my other clients and get my work done. I feel like if I spent all my time actively avoiding it, that would mean it's controlling me, right? 

I just want to face things maturely and move on. Choosing to focus on the present is the responsible thing to do, don't you think? I really hope I'm approaching this the right way.
Are there any activities or places you've been avoiding because they remind you of the incident with the upset client?

Um, avoiding places? No, no, I wouldn't say that. I mean, I still go into the office every day, just like normal. I haven't taken any time off or anything like that. I really want to be reliable, you know? 

I guess I haven't been taking my lunch breaks in the front lobby area where... where it happened. But that's just because I've been so busy with tax season coming up, I've just been eating at my desk to catch up on paperwork. It's just more efficient that way, really. 

I'm definitely not hiding out or avoiding anyone. I just want to make sure I'm staying on top of my workload and being a good employee. That's the best way to move past something like this, right? Just keeping your nose to the grindstone and staying productive?
Do you feel like you're often in a daze or spaced out when these episodes of feeling unreal happen?

Well, um... "in a daze" makes it sound a little bit like I'm slacking off or losing my grip, and I definitely don't want you to think that. I'm still very sharp with my work. But... I guess, to be completely honest, part of what brought me in to see you is that I keep having these moments where... well, where my own house or the office just feels completely unreal. 

It's hard to explain without sounding a little, you know, crazy... but it's almost like I'm watching myself from across the room instead of actually being there. Just for a moment, you know? I always snap right back to it and get back to work. I mean, it's probably just fatigue from staring at tax forms all day, right? I really hope that doesn't sound too bizarre. I'm still totally capable, I promise. Does that make sense?
Do you feel like you're observing yourself from outside your body during these episodes of feeling unreal?

Oh, gosh, no. I... I didn't mean it literally like that. "Outside my body" makes it sound a little too much like some kind of sci-fi movie or... or a hallucination, and I definitely don't want you to think I'm losing touch with reality. I'm very grounded, I promise. 

When I said watching from across the room, it was really more of a... a figure of speech, I guess? It's just a brief feeling of being disconnected, not like I'm literally floating around looking down at myself. I'm definitely still in my own skin. I just... I really hope I didn't give you the wrong impression with how I explained it before. I'm trying my best to describe it properly, so... does that clarify things a bit?
Do you feel like you're disconnected from yourself or your surroundings when these episodes happen?

Yes, I suppose disconnected is a really good way to put it. Like I was trying to explain a minute ago, it's really just those moments where my own house or the office suddenly feels completely unreal, almost like a movie set or something. And I get that strange sense of detachment from myself, like that feeling of watching myself from across the room that I brought up earlier. 

But it's very brief, and I always stay perfectly professional through it, I swear. I really hope I'm making sense and not sounding too unstable. It's just a little embarrassing to admit to having these weird disconnected moments when I'm normally so focused and grounded. That's a fairly normal reaction to stress, though, isn't it?
Are there any other situations or activities that you've been avoiding since the incident with the upset client?

Oh, no... no, definitely not. I mean, I wouldn't let something like that stop me from doing my job or living my life. I'm still coming into the office every single day, still going out to grab my usual coffee, still doing my regular routine. 

I really try to just push through and be reliable. I don't want you to think I'm just... hiding away from the world or neglecting my responsibilities, because I'm absolutely not. I think it's important to keep pushing forward and not let things get the better of you, don't you agree? I'm really trying to handle it the right way, so... I hope that shows I'm managing okay.
How often do you experience these feelings of disconnection from yourself or your surroundings?

Oh, um... I haven't really kept a tally or anything like that. It's... it's really not that often, I promise. Maybe just, I don't know, a handful of times since that whole thing happened with the client? It's definitely not a daily occurrence. 

And like I said, it never gets in the way of my tax prep work or anything. I just... I wouldn't want you to think I'm zoning out all the time or losing my grip. It's just a fleeting thing every now and then when things get a bit overwhelming. That's a pretty normal amount to experience something like that, wouldn't you say? I mean, I assume most people wouldn't even notice it if they were as busy as I am, right?
Are there any aspects of your daily life that you're avoiding because they remind you of the incident with the upset client?

Um, no, not really. Like I think I touched on a second ago, I'm... I'm really making a conscious effort to just keep everything as normal as possible. I still drive the exact same route to the office, still go to the same places for lunch... I wouldn't want to let one bad afternoon dictate how I live my life, you know? 

I feel like if I started avoiding normal, everyday things, that's when it would mean I wasn't coping well, and I definitely don't want to go down that road. So I'm just making sure I face it all head-on and keep up with my regular schedule. That is the healthiest way to handle it, isn't it? I really want to make sure I'm doing the right things to get past this, and I figure staying productive is the best way to show I'm bouncing back.
